Source-backed finding

Appen — reported revenue. The audited FY2025 statements report consolidated customer-contract revenue of USD 230.774 million for 1 January–31 December 2025, including Appen Global USD 127.874 million and Appen China USD 102.900 million. These geographic operating segments do not isolate expert generative-AI data or the market definition used in this report. The figures are full-year reported revenue, not annualized pace, gross transaction volume, contributor pay or a comparable human-feedback segment across suppliers.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025, candidate.supplier.appen.segments-fy2025

Source-backed finding

Proximal — annualized pace. Its 29 September 2026 announcement reports $200 million in annualized revenue. The inspected disclosure does not specify an ISO currency code, annualization window, gross-versus-net basis or revenue split by business line. It is self-reported pace, not an audited annual revenue total, profit, bookings, valuation or contractor payout. No annual recognized-revenue amount is calculated from it in this report.

Evidence: repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure

Source-backed finding

Scale — cumulative contributor payout. Its FY2025 statement, approved in June 2026, reports nearly $1 billion paid to hundreds of thousands of contributors across more than 150 countries to date. The statement does not define a start/end period or a dollar currency code for that aggregate, and payment reconciliation was not inspected. The number is not annual revenue, annual labor cost, a current paid-active workforce total or a wage estimate.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout

Source-backed finding

Labelbox — financing and valuation. The 14 October 2026 company announcement reports more than $100 million in Series E financing comprising equity and a credit facility, at a $1.25 billion pre-money valuation. The inspected source uses dollar symbols without an explicit ISO currency. The facility is not equity, and financing and valuation are not revenue or evidence of accepted data volume. No implied annual growth or provider-performance score is calculated.

Evidence: candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing

Source-backed finding

Prolific — tariff and reward rules. The captured FAQ states usual platform fees of 42.8% for corporate customers and 33.3% for academic/nonprofit customers, but the bound passage does not explicitly state the percentage denominator. It separately sets minimum participant rewards of GBP 6 or USD 8 per hour and recommends GBP 9 or USD 12, with higher expert compensation recommended. Managed services are custom-priced. These are published rules and tariff disclosures rather than realized earnings, margins or a complete specialist-project quote.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.prolific.fees, candidate.supplier.prolific.minimum-rewards

Source-backed finding

Other disclosed billing units differ. Prime Intellect’s Model Factory terms meter allocated GPU-hours prorated to the second, with rates in the order or platform; personnel post-training needs a separate professional-services order. A.Team lists hourly and other builder-engagement models. Terac describes expert payout plus a platform fee and separately monthly USD payment per verified completion for partnerships. AfterQuery reserves fees to order forms or separate agreements. These documents describe commercial structure, not a comparable price per accepted preference pair or environment.

Evidence: repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.gpu-billing-basis, candidate.cohort4.prime_intellect.professional-service-separation, candidate.cohort5.a-team.delivery-model, candidate.cohort5.terac.buyer-billing-model, candidate.cohort5.terac.partner-payment-basis, candidate.cohort4.afterquery.separate-service-pricing

Analysis

The analytical rule is to keep commercial denominators separate. A company-wide annualized rate cannot be divided by a benchmark count to estimate task price; cumulative payouts cannot identify a current take rate; financing cannot measure demand; a broad expert pool cannot be a capacity denominator. The selected disclosures support questions for diligence, not supplier market shares. A defensible future comparison would need the same reporting period, currency, gross/net basis, organizational segment and accepted-unit definition across every included provider.

Evidence: candidate.supplier.appen.revenue-fy2025, repair.binding.v1.candidate.cohort4.proximal.annualized-revenue-disclosure, candidate.supplier.scale_ai.cumulative-payout, candidate.cohort2.labelbox.financing, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.candidate.supplier.mercor.expert-pool

Method

Reproducible buyer calculation: accepted-unit cost equals all attributable project cash costs divided by independently accepted units. The numerator should state whether it includes recruitment, qualification, paid training, tool licenses, compute, project management, review, rework and buyer-side acceptance. The denominator should identify the unit: independent judgment, resolved item, trajectory, verified environment, recorded hour or licensed release. This is a proposed accounting method; the report does not insert hypothetical numbers or claim observed costs for suppliers.

Method

Reproducible review calculation: first-pass acceptance equals accepted units on first submission divided by all submitted units; final acceptance equals accepted units after permitted rework divided by all submitted units. Keep attempt, exclusion and unresolved counts. For expert-time projects, report both accepted outputs per paid hour and buyer QA effort per accepted output, without interpreting either as worker wages. For environment projects, separate authoring, maintenance, execution and recurring license costs, and preserve the term of access.

Method

Procurement comparison procedure: issue the same task brief and acceptance rubric, obtain responsibility and rights schedules, run a paid calibration sample, then quote a frozen production scope. Compare totals only after normalizing included review/rework and access terms. Log scope changes as new versions rather than treating a renegotiated specification as supplier underperformance. Proposed service-level thresholds should come from the buyer’s loss tolerance and pilot uncertainty; they are not reported market standards.

Research gap

The commercial research gap is task-matched economics. This corpus does not supply comparable current contracts, realized gross/net human-data revenue, project margins, cancellation/rework charges or accepted-unit costs across suppliers. Missing financial disclosure is unknown rather than zero. No financial forecast, market-size projection, provider-return model or inferred valuation multiple is warranted by this evidence.

Analysis

Cost comparisons must include the measured boundary. LMCrowd excludes model, prompt and worker selection from its tariff comparison; CrowdAgent holds human annotation proportions rather than all computation or operating cost equal. HelpSteer2 discards about half of collected annotations overall, so accepted responses and purchased ratings have different denominators. Request setup, failed/rejected work, QA, adjudication, model calls, compute and accepted-unit totals explicitly. These studies inform accounting questions; they do not provide current service prices or a cross-provider cost ranking.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.lmcrowd.cost-boundary, cohort9.claim.crowdagent.fixed-human-ratios, cohort9.claim.helpsteer2.agreement-selection

Analysis

Worker-time accounting is also distinct from project billing. The historical MTurk log study produces different work-unit rates under accept-to-submit and temporal-cluster definitions; its task/cluster medians are not median worker wages. Selected plugin users, unknown active effort and noncausal associations constrain inference. For a new project, request consented, task-appropriate compensation and time evidence rather than convert historical platform figures or supplier revenue into a claim about present worker earnings.

Evidence: cohort9.claim.earnings.wage-definition, cohort9.claim.earnings.work-unit-wages, cohort9.claim.earnings.causality-limit

Analysis

Cost comparison must preserve generation, verification and acceptance budgets. Weaver generates 100 candidates per query and can call many verifiers; APEX-SWE averages repeated one-hour task runs; APEX-Agents evaluates repeated attempts; DAYJOB excludes error attempts from its score and uses creator-estimated healthcare time and a separately reported finance mean. These choices affect measured performance and a buyer’s cost ledger differently. Confidence is high that a single score or token bill is insufficient and unestablished for relative supplier unit costs. Record all attempted work, retries, judge calls, human escalation and accepted outputs before estimating a project-specific cost per usable unit. DAYJOB’s reported agent/condenser call cost excludes the judge and is not an all-in service price.

Evidence: mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2506.18203.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2506.18203.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2506.18203.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2506.18203.result, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.08806.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.08806.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.08806.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.08806.result, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.14242.limitation, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.14242.method, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.14242.provenance, mandatory2.claim.arxiv.2601.14242.result, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.01306.limitation, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.01306.method, repair.qualbinding.20261111.v1.mandatory3.claim.arxiv.2610.01306.result

Analysis

Reported professional-task performance is not revenue or observed economic output. DAYJOB’s healthcare times are creator estimates; its finance mean has a separate dataset-card basis; APEX-Accounting measures rubric completion and repeated reliability on selected synthetic worlds; PLE reports a mean hybrid score. Multiplying those scores by an occupation’s wages would introduce unmeasured task representativeness, deployment overhead, review, failure cost and acceptance assumptions. Confidence is high in rejecting that conversion from this evidence. Prospective matched deployments with observed professional time, complete exception costs and verified accepted deliverables would be needed to change the economic conclusion. DAYJOB’s reported agent/condenser call cost excludes the judge and is not an all-in service price.

Source-backed finding

Datatang / Nexdata group — unaudited six-month revenue. The issuer reports operating revenue of RMB 180,323,485.50 for January 1–June 30, 2026, and explicitly labels the report unaudited. The reported group ownership table includes Nexdata entities. This is group revenue for that period, not a standalone Nexdata segment figure, a run rate, task price or gross customer spend.

Evidence: candidate.mandatory14.datatang.crowdsourced-training-data-production, candidate.mandatory14.datatang.group-dedup-ownership, candidate.mandatory14.datatang.issuer-identity, candidate.mandatory14.datatang.japanese-brand-identity, candidate.mandatory14.datatang.licensed-resource-service, candidate.mandatory14.datatang.reported-revenue2026h1

Analysis

Budget comparison — a timed run, a valid scored attempt and a billable production unit can diverge. DeepSWE excludes provider/verifier/network errors without resampling but counts timeouts as failures; GeneBench-Pro excludes execution/format errors and uses unequal attempted-run budgets for some configurations; HCAST’s human baseline combines hourly rates and performance incentives. Confidence is high that these denominators must be retained and unestablished for a common accepted-unit cost. A buyer should reconcile all attempts, provider charges, human time, reruns and independently accepted outputs. Prospective matched project ledgers would change a unit-cost assessment.

Analysis

The new reasoning-data disclosures add unlike cost units to the commercial ledger. Bespoke describes about $800 and 1.5 hours for synthetic dataset generation, while Light-R1 estimates about $1,000 and under six hours on twelve H800s for training. Generation expense and training estimates are different cost boundaries, and neither is a current supplier quote or a fully reconciled accepted-item cost. HackerRank’s submission library and challenge registrations describe yet other units, with no disclosed delivered-training-record price. Confidence is high that these figures must remain separate and unestablished for economic superiority. A buyer would need complete compute, human review, licensing, rejection, retry and acceptance accounting under the same deliverable definition before making a cost comparison.
